title: Only about 1 in 5 newborn deaths is captured
plain_language: The system logged an average of over 8,500 newborn deaths a year, but roughly 48,000 are expected, so most deaths never make it into the routine record.
so_what: Policymakers planning newborn care are working from numbers that understate the problem by more than 75%.

title: Reporting is barely above half
plain_language: Hospitals filed their monthly newborn-death reports only 58.3% of the time. Regional hospitals hit a median of 61.7%; tertiary hospitals just 50%.
so_what: If a hospital doesn't file, its babies vanish from the national picture, and blanks get counted as missing, not zero.

title: No tertiary hospital cleared the 75% bar
plain_language: Only 8 of 28 regional hospitals reported in more than 75% of months. None of the 7 tertiary hospitals did; the best managed 73.3%.
so_what: Tertiary hospitals handle the sickest newborns, so their gaps hide some of the highest-risk deaths.

title: Most hospitals' rates don't hold together
plain_language: Only 28.6% of hospitals had year-to-year newborn death rates that stayed within WHO's plus-or-minus 33% consistency band for 2021-2023.
so_what: Wildly swinging numbers signal reporting problems, not real changes in how many babies are dying.

title: 5.9 vs 24 per 1,000
plain_language: After adjusting for home births, the system's 2024 newborn death rate was 5.9 per 1,000 live births, about a quarter of the survey figure of 24 and the UN's 21.
so_what: The routine system looks far rosier than reality, which can create false confidence.

title: The best regional hospitals show it can work
plain_language: The 28% of regional hospitals that reported in over 75% of months also reported higher, more realistic death rates (over 100 per 1,000 admitted babies).
so_what: High performers show good routine data is achievable, and give the rest a model to copy.

title: Two systems, different answers
plain_language: Three regional hospitals consistently reported higher newborn death rates in DHIS2 than in the detailed NID database; one tertiary hospital matched closely in 2023-2024.
so_what: Cross-checking against a second dataset reveals which facilities over- or under-count.

title: Ten years, 1.4 million births, 34,190 deaths
plain_language: The study covers 2015 to 2024 across 35 hospitals: over 1.4 million institutional births and 34,190 recorded newborn deaths.
so_what: It's one of the most comprehensive looks at newborn-death data quality in a low-income setting.
